Dynamics of Microvillus Extension and Tether Formation in Rolling Leukocytes. P-selectin glycoprotein ligand-1 (PSGL-1) binding to P-selectin mediates leukocyte rolling under conditions of flow. In human neutrophils, a type of leukocyte belonging to the innate immune system, PSGL-1 molecules are located on the neutrophil's surface ruffles, called microvilli. Each newly formed P-selectin-PSGL-1 bond can become load bearing, imposing on its microvillus a pulling force that deforms the microvillus. Depending on the magnitude of the bond force, a microvillus can be extended, or a thin membrane cylinder (a tether) can be formed at the tip of the microvillus.
